subject: cfa in lavaan recognize incorrectly frequencies of categorical variables

messages.author: c185bf1eab54b5fd
messages.subject: cfa in lavaan recognize incorrectly frequencies of categorical variables
parts:
Hi, I am running a simple cfa with  two categorical variables (pos and workstatus) and 2 continuous variables (lincome and lwh):
ctrl.labor <- "
control_labor =~ pos+lincome+lwh+workstatus"

I notify categorical variables by these commands:
X180108_lkh$pos <- ordered(X180108_lkh$pos)
X180108_lkh$workstatus <- ordered(X180108_lkh$workstatus)

I run this
> fit.l <- cfa(ctrl.labor, data=X180108_lkh)

However, I receive an error like this: 
"Error in lav_samplestats_step1(Y = Data, ov.names = ov.names, ov.types = ov.types,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: some categories of variable `workstatus' are empty in group 1; frequencies are [0 8064 13291]"

Frequency of variable "workstatus" is
> table(X180108_lkh$workstatus)
    1     2     3 
  184  8064 13301
==> There is no empty category in this variable. I dont know why lavaan recognizes frequencies as [0 8064 13291 while they are actually [  184  8064 13301]

Please help me to solve this situation
Thank you very much

messages.subject: Re: cfa in lavaan recognize incorrectly frequencies of categorical variables
parts: Do you have incomplete data for other variables? The default is listwise deletion, which could have knocked out all cases for the first response category.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: cfa in lavaan recognize incorrectly frequencies of categorical variables
parts:
On 02/05/2018 01:51 PM, Edward Rigdon wrote:
> Do you have incomplete data for other variables? The default is listwise
> deletion, which could have knocked out all cases for the first response
> category.

Indeed. Using missing = "pairwise" may solve this.

Yves.

messages.author: c185bf1eab54b5fd
messages.subject: Re: cfa in lavaan recognize incorrectly frequencies of categorical variables
parts:
Dear Edward Rigdon and Yves Rosseel,
You are right that this problem is caused by missing data. I haven't try missing="pairwise" yet, so I drop "workstatus" as an incidcator, now in my model, there are 3 indicators (pos+lincome+lwh) and then, with theoretical modification, I use "workstatus" as an exogenous variable predicting the latent variable "control_labor". And it works.
I will try to pairwise later.
Thank you very much,
Dai
